name: How to Spot a Bad Cabinet Repair

step.name: Step 1
step.text: When you're getting your cabinets repaired, you want to make sure the fix is going to last and not just cover up a bigger issue. There are definitely some warning signs that a repair might not be up to snuff. A big red flag is if the repair person only focuses on cosmetic issues without investigating the underlying cause of the damage. For example, simply patching a chipped finish without addressing why it chipped in the first place might mean the problem resurfaces quickly. Also, if they're trying to repair structural damage, like badly warped or water-damaged wood, with a quick fix, that’s a sign to be cautious. These issues often need more than just a surface-level repair; they might indicate it's time for a replacement. Another mistake is overlooking weak frames, sagging shelves, or broken hinges. These aren’t minor aesthetic problems; they point to deeper structural failure that a good repair should address. If the repair doesn’t fully restore function and appearance, or if the cabinet isn’t structurally sound afterward, you’ve likely got a bad repair on your hands. Always ensure your professional fully inspects the damage and confirms the cabinet's integrity after the work is done.
